name: Vinaceous-Slate
lede: Vinaceous-Slate is a dark, wine-tinged grey, Robert Ridgway's 1912 pairing of his "vinaceous" naming scheme with the plain grey of slate rock.

sections.title: A wine-tinted slate
sections.body:
Ridgway plated this hue in 1912 at plate L, hue 69'''', tone i, and the ISCC-NBS system later filed it as block 228, a dark purplish grey [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[graphite-violet]], [[heliotrope-slate]], [[grebe]] and [[blackish-grey]], at 3.6, 3.6, 
In our library it is an exact color match to [[smoke]] itself (CIEDE2000 0.0) [2]. Its nearest distinct neighbors are [[graphite-violet]] and [[heliotrope-slate]], both almost the same at a distance of 3.6 [2]. Measured in LCH it is lightness 41, chroma 3 and hue 358 degrees, nearly neutral [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this grey in 271 of 23,781 paintings (1.14%, as photographed), more common than 63% of the named colors we track [3]. It most often plays a shadow, in 35% of its 135 strongest matches [3]. It is also most over-represented in paintings from India, at 3.1 times the expected rate [3]. The earliest dated match runs to 1119, nearly eight centuries before Ridgway's own 1912 record; the match is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof the pigment was there, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [3].

origin.source: Ridgway, Color Standards and Color Nomenclature
